title: Oct 28 Results: Sometimes Baseball Breaks Your Heart
summary: A tough 0-1 day as our Rays prediction missed the mark—here's what happened.

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About Baseball

Some days, the numbers look perfect. The matchup seems clear. Everything points in one direction. And then baseball reminds you why we love this game—because anything can happen.

Oct 28 gave us exactly one game to analyze, and unfortunately, we didn't get it right. But that's the beauty and the heartbreak of this sport all rolled into one.

## The Game That Got Away

We liked the Rays at home with a 57% win probability against the Brewers. It wasn't a slam-dunk prediction—57% tells you it's close—but the numbers suggested Tampa Bay had the edge.

The Brewers had other ideas. They came into Tropicana Field and took care of business, proving once again that probabilities are guides, not guarantees.

## What We Learned

A 0-1 day stings, there's no sugarcoating it. But here's what matters: we're transparent about every pick, every result. The wins and the losses.

When you're picking games based on data and probabilities, you're going to have days like this. A 57% probability means there's a 43% chance the other team wins—and today, that 43% came through. That's not an excuse; it's just baseball.

The key is staying disciplined, trusting the process, and learning from what the data tells us after the fact.

content.title: 📅 Tomorrow's Schedule
content.sub: Time to rest, reset, and get ready for the next slate

content.value:
## The Road Ahead

With no games scheduled for tomorrow, we've got time to dig deeper into the trends, refine our models, and come back stronger. Every miss is a chance to get better.

That's the thing about following baseball over a full season—it's a marathon, not a sprint. One tough day doesn't define us. How we respond does.

We'll be back with fresh analysis when the games resume. Until then, keep the faith, trust the process, and remember: even the best hitters fail seven out of ten times.

*See you at the next first pitch,*

*— Hana*
